explanation: Let length[i] be the longest nondecreasing subsequence ending exactly at index i. Test each earlier j with A[j]≤A[i] and extend its best subsequence. The final answer is the maximum over all endings.
timeComplexity: O(n²): the nested loops examine all earlier endpoints. Tail-array versions binary-search once per entry; endpoint-DP versions compare all earlier positions.
spaceComplexity: O(n) endpoint lengths. The tails list or endpoint-length array has at most n entries.

correctness: A nontrivial subsequence ending at i has a preceding endpoint j<i with A[j]≤A[i]. The recurrence tries all such j and can attain each extension. The singleton gives length one when no predecessor qualifies. Therefore the computed endpoint optimum, and its global maximum, are exact.
walkthrough: For [3,1,1,2], endpoint lengths are [1,1,2,3]: the second 1 extends the first 1, and 2 extends that length-two subsequence. Return 3. The walkthroughCase uses the judge’s JSON input format and expected observation.
edgeCases: Equal values may all belong to the subsequence.
